question.text: If the distance between the plane \(a x-2 y+z=k\) and the plane containing the lines \(\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}\) and \(\frac{x-2}{3}=\frac{y-3}{4}=\frac{z-4}{5}\) is \(\sqrt{6}\), then \(|k|\) is

solution.text:
Hint: Equation of plane
\(\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x-1 & y-2 & z-3 \\
2 & 3 & 4 \\
3 & 4 & 5
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x-2 y+z=0 \quad ---(1)
\end{aligned}\)
& given \(\alpha x-2 y+z=k\)  ---(2)
(1) // (2) \(\Rightarrow \alpha=1, k \neq 0\)
\(\therefore \frac{|k|}{\sqrt{6}}=\sqrt{6} \Rightarrow|k|=6\)
